messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: alternative parameterizations of cutpoints/simplex
parts:
This came up on stan-users.

On 11/16/12 8:23 PM, Ben Goodrich wrote:

> Actually, instead of rescaling and / or relocating a simplex, it might work better to consider
> the cumulative sum of a
> simplex to be chunks of the logistic CDF. If you feed those into the inverse CDF, which is known in the case of the
> logistic distribution, then you get cutpoints out.

We can fiddle with the transforms for ordered vars
and for simplexes. Now that I see how important these
geometric decisions are, I keep wondering if we can
find better-behaved general transforms than what we use
now. Andrew -- this is another kind of exploration that
could be good for a grad student because I could easily
see it leading to a neat self-contained paper.

> thank you. just want to clarify that there is not a cumsum function in stan returning a vector. i will then write
> it in the stan script (in the absence of partial indexing).

I added cumulative_sum() function to the to-do list. We've
seen it a few times, so might as well have it. I'm going
to go on a function-writing binge because the requests
are stacking up.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Rtools only 32 bit?
parts:
g++ itself is a 32-bit program from Rtools? Can it
still compile 64-bit executables for 64-bit R?

The 32-bit limitation is really too bad because of the
amount of memory we want in the compiler. This could
be very limiting for Windows users.

Is there somewhere we can point people to get instructions
on swappin gin a 64-bit compiler?

- Bob

On 12/28/12 9:51 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> Just to point out that the gcc in Rtools is 32 bits program, which cannot take advantage of all the RAM in a 64 bits OS.

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Rtools only 32 bit?
parts:
By default, the gcc in rtools generated 32 bit exe code.  We can show that by using the file.exe command in rtools\bin.
See the following examples.

C:\Users\root\Desktop>type a.c
#include <stdio.h>

int main() {
  printf("H.\n");
  return 0;
}

C:\Users\root\Desktop>c:\rtools\gcc-4.6.3\bin\gcc a.c

C:\Users\root\Desktop>c:\rtools\bin\file a.exe
a.exe: PE32 executable for MS Windows (console) Intel 80386 32-bit

C:\Users\root\Desktop>c:\rtools\gcc-4.6.3\bin\gcc -m64 a.c

C:\Users\root\Desktop>c:\rtools\bin\file a.exe
a.exe: PE32+ executable for MS Windows (console) Mono/.Net assembly


--
Jiqiang

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Rtools only 32 bit?
parts:
Theoretically it is doable and it is easy to download some 64-bit gcc toolchains 
from http://sourceforge.net/projects/mingw-w64/files/Toolchains%20targetting%20Win64/Personal%20Builds/rubenvb/gcc-4.7-release/ and a lot of other places. 

But most of those that can be downloaded are supporting only either 32bit target or 64bits target.  I guess that is not a problem for an individual.  But without much testing, I am sure enough those are compatible with R for some reason as in my limited experience, I have a 64 bits compiler that can compile models' in RStan but it cranes R.  

--
Jiqiang

On Sat, Dec 29, 2012 at 2:20 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

on swappin gin a 64-bit compiler?

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Rtools only 32 bit?
parts:
This is not necessary for R 64 bits on windows since the makefiles used for R CMD SHLIB has -m64 flag.  It is just that gcc itself is 32 bits, which seems to easily have memory issues under -O0. 

--
Jiqiang

Maybe have set_cppo() add -m64 to CFLAGS on Windows iff R.version$arch indicates the machine is 64bit?

This is not necessary for R 64 bits on windows since the makefiles used for R CMD SHLIB has -m64 flag.  It is just that gcc itself is 32 bits, which seems to easily have memory issues under -O0.

Okay, well maybe that is another reason to document the possibility of O=s. There was also a post

Ben
